newsitem.title: USA: Freddie Mac to sell Philip Morris bonds - lawmaker.
newsitem.headline: Freddie Mac to sell Philip Morris bonds - lawmaker.

text.p: The Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp (Freddie Mac) has decided to sell its bonds in Philip Morris, U.S. House Banking Committee Chairman James Leach said late on Thursday.
"Freddie Mac's common-sense decision to sell its Philip Morris bonds is welcomed," Leach, a Republican from Iowa, said in a statement.
Officials at Freddie Mac were not immediately available to comment on Leach's statement.
Leach last week launched an attack on Freddie Mac for borrowing from the Treasury at concessionary rates and using the money for non-mortgage investments, including Philip Morris bonds.
In his latest statement, Leach repeated his opposition to non-mortgage investments by Freddie Mac, saying they fell outside its charter to assist housing.
"To the degree Freddie Mac needs to make liquidity investments, the most appropriate investment would appear to be government bonds," Leach said.
